newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt and futures get boost from U.S. debt.
newsitem.headline: German debt and futures get boost from U.S. debt.

text.p: German Bunds and futures were firmer in late dealings on Tuesday, getting a boost from the U.S. debt market in the absence of fresh domestic fundamentals to push the market in either direction, traders said.

DTB September Bund futures were up 34 basis points at 101.86 and near the session high of 101.89 in late dealings, while the 10-year cash 6.00 percent Bund due July 2007 was at 102.43 with a yield of 5.67 percent.
"The U.S. is the reason for the late gains since the market has otherwise lacked ideas on how to trade," said one Frankfurt dealer. "The market was generally adrift for the day."
German debt market dealings are expected to remain within a range ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve's policy meeting that ends on Wednesday.
Traders said DTB September Bund futures would find resistance at 101.89 and support at 101.40, which should remain the parameters for near-term dealings.
The German market generally shrugged off news that Bonn sold the first tranche of its 30-year bond even though past 30-year bonds led to market tops for 10-year issues.
"The offering has generally been priced into the market," said one dealer.

Dealers also said the market ignored comments from European leaders calling for a strict interpretation of the Maastricht Treaty in picking members for the single European currency, saying the comments were nothing new for the market.

Instead, the main reason for late gains came from rising U.S. debt prices that were boosted by a relatively soft reading of the June NAPM index at 55.7 compard with expectations for an index level of 56.4.
